messages:
inc-bot: :loud_sound: PAGER: Autoscaling alert in prod-eu-west for GPU pool 'gpu-render'. metric: custom/pod_queue_length > 3000 for 6m. Severity=P1. Pager: oncall-ml

oncall-ml: I'm on it. Seeing queue_count spike and ingress 429s. Realtime requests piling up on gpu-router. 

sre-hannah: joining. Any signs from prometheus-adapter or metrics-server? Last incident looked similar (metric ingestion delay).

oncall-ml: prometheus-adapter shows timeout to metrics-server + rapid enqueue growth. Logs: ```2026-03-15T12:02:11Z WARN http: upstream timeout from metrics-server
2026-03-15T12:02:12Z ERROR queue: enqueue failed: max_size_reached
2026-03-15T12:02:18Z ERROR handler: serve_custom_metrics failed: no data```

infra-raj: kube events show metrics-server OOMKilled on node-kube-09 at 12:00. It restarted but readiness probe failing intermittently. Node also reported memory pressure on system reserved.

eng-ops-kim: customer impact: high-priority endpoints for 'streaming' models are getting 503/429s. Support, please surface affected tenants.

support-nora: Noted. Reached out to top impacted accounts: content-gen-co, ad-tech-llm, analyticsx. They're seeing retries and timeouts since ~12:03 UTC. Escalating to CSMs.

sre-hannah: quick mitigation idea: 1) cordon batch nodes to stop new batch GPU jobs from scheduling 2) scale gpu-render pool manually 3) restart prometheus-adapter with increased queue and enable backpressure 4) apply emergency HPA annotation to use last-known metric snapshot. Who can run kube ops?

oncall-ml: I can run the commands. Starting with cordon: `kubectl cordon node-gpu-batch-03` -> cordoned.

oncall-ml: manual scale attempt: `kubectl -n compute scale deploy/gpu-render --replicas=8` -> output: scaled. Some pods stuck Pending waiting for nodes.

infra-raj: launching additional GPU nodes in the pool now. Provider estimate ~5-7m. Also checking quota; may need manual override.

sre-hannah: while infra provisions, let's fall back non-latency-critical traffic to cpu-render cluster. eng-ops, can you toggle routing rule?

eng-ops-kim: toggling feature flag to divert 'batch-infer' route to cpu-render: `/flags route.batch-infer -> cpu-render` applied. Expect batch jobs to failover. 

support-nora: customers confirm some reduction in 429s but still seeing intermittent errors for streaming calls. 

oncall-ml: restarted prometheus-adapter deployment with env ADAPTER_QUEUE_SIZE=10000 and ADAPTER_BACKPRESSURE=true. Logs: ```2026-03-15T12:09:45Z INFO adapter: startup complete; queue_capacity=10000
2026-03-15T12:09:56Z INFO adapter: backlog=4200 -> processing...```

sre-hannah: apply HPA emergency annotation: `kubectl annotate hpa/gpu-render autoscale.redwood.com/emergency-force=true --overwrite` This will use cached desiredReplicas.

oncall-ml: annotation applied. HPA controller reports desiredReplicas=7 (forced).

infra-raj: new nodes provisioning: 2 ready now, 2 provisioning, 2 failed due to quota. Raising ticket with cloud-ops for quota bump.

eng-ops-kim: FYI, routing diversion caused increased latency on cpu-render but kept critical paths alive. We may need to throttle non-essential endpoints to reduce overall pressure. Suggest applying a ResourceQuota to 'ingest' namespace to limit GPU usage.

sre-hannah: agreed. I'll add a temporary network-level rate limiter on gpu-router to cap per-tenant QPS for non-SLAs.

support-nora: CSMs asking for timeline and mitigation details. Sending a short note: we're mitigating, autoscaling pipeline degraded due to metrics ingestion failure, engineers actively scaling and routing to reduce impact. ETA 20-30m.

pm-tomas: marking incident P1 and notifying legal for ad-tech-llm due to data processing SLA. Please capture exact error windows for post-incident report.

oncall-ml: adapter backlog dropping: 4200 -> 900 over 8m. metrics-server readiness passing on node-kube-09 after memory bump and restart: `kubectl -n kube-system set resources deploy/metrics-server --limits=memory=600Mi` then rollout.

infra-raj: bumped metrics-server memory and adjusted liveness probe threshold. Also added a nodeSelector to keep metrics-server off memory-constrained nodes. Applying helm chart update.

sre-hannah: monitoring HPA: custom metrics flow restored. HPA observed desiredReplicas scaling from 7 down to 5 as queue decreases. Good sign.

eng-ops-kim: cloud-ops increased quota for GPUs; remaining Pending pods are now scheduling. Provider reports nodes coming up in 3 min.

support-nora: customers reporting improved success rates, some still observing higher latency during in-flight sessions. 

sre-hannah: next steps before we close pager: 1) confirm adapter steady-state <200 queue 2) ensure all critical pods Ready 3) remove emergency force annotation 4) document timeline and affected tenants.

oncall-ml: confirm adapter queue=120 and stable. All gpu-render pods Ready=5/5. Removing annotation: `kubectl annotate hpa/gpu-render autoscale.redwood.com/emergency-force-` -> annotation removed.

pm-tomas: PM note: please include runbook gaps—metrics-server memory defaults too low and no automated backpressure config. We'll follow up for permanent fixes.

sre-hannah: action items assigned: - infra to ship metrics-server resource bump and adjust helm defaults (raj) - eng to add adapter backpressure metrics and alert (kim) - devexp to update oncall runbook with QoS toggle steps and HPA emergency annotation procedure (sre-hannah) - support to assemble customer impact list (nora)

oncall-ml: handing off to SRE for monitoring. Handoff: oncall-ml -> sre-hannah. Last state: adapter q=120, HPA desired=5 current=5, extra nodes active. Removing pager.

sre-hannah: taking incident. Bridge open for 45m monitoring then RCA. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark: 

inc-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Severity lowered to P2 at 12:47 UTC. Full timeline and notes saved to /incidents/3612345678.
